high.title: IPCA-15: Inflation Preview Advances 0.62% in May, Above Expectations, and Breaks Through BC's 4.5% Target Ceiling
high.summary: Brazil's inflation preview (IPCA-15) rose 0.62% in May, significantly above market expectations of 0.56%, with 12-month accumulated inflation reaching 4.64% - breaching the Central Bank's 4.5% target ceiling. While monthly inflation decelerated from April's 0.89%, the annual rate accelerated from 4.37% previously. Food and beverages led the increase at 1.38%, followed by Housing (1.03%) and Health/Personal Care (1.05%). This inflation overshoot is critical for FX and bond markets as it increases pressure on the Central Bank to maintain or raise the Selic rate, which markets already expect to reach 13.25% by end-2026. Higher inflation above target supports a hawkish BCB stance, potentially strengthening BRL in the medium term but pressuring government bond prices. The overshoot also complicates the government's fiscal framework adherence and may influence COPOM's next decision.

high.title: Brazil Registers Current Account Deficit of US$ 1.8 Billion in April, More Negative Balance Than Market Expected
high.summary: Brazil's current account deficit reached US$ 1.765 billion in April, substantially wider than Reuters consensus of US$ 200 million, with the 12-month rolling deficit now representing 2.66% of GDP. The primary income account deficit expanded to US$ 6.801 billion from US$ 5.018 billion year-over-year, while the trade surplus improved to US$ 9.707 billion from US$ 6.957 billion in April 2024. The services deficit also widened to US$ 5.044 billion. This larger-than-expected current account deficit puts pressure on BRL funding needs and external financing requirements. However, the Central Bank noted that foreign direct investment exceeded expectations (though specific figures weren't provided in the excerpt), which could help finance the deficit. The deteriorating current account balance is negative for BRL fundamentals and increases Brazil's dependence on portfolio flows to maintain external equilibrium.

medium.title: Ibovespa Falls with Risk Aversion Focused on Middle East; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (26)
medium.summary: Ibovespa opened down 0.93% to 176,154 points due to renewed risk aversion over US-Iran tensions, while USD/BRL fell 0.12% to R$ 5.0131 following dollar weakness abroad. The Chamber of Deputies postponed voting on the constitutional amendment to end the 6x1 work schedule. Market sentiment was affected by geopolitical tensions impacting risk appetite globally.

medium.title: Ibovespa Rises with New Wave of Optimism About Middle East and Ignores Above-Expected IPCA-15; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (27)
medium.summary: Ibovespa traded up 0.47% to 177,420 points on improved investor sentiment over US-Iran peace negotiation progress, offsetting concerns about higher-than-expected IPCA-15 inflation data. USD/BRL rose 0.53% to R$ 5.0538 despite dollar weakness internationally. The market focused more on geopolitical developments than domestic inflation pressures.

medium.title: Empiricus Issues 'Alert' on Its Recommended Stocks to Seek Extra Income: Petrobras (PETR4) and Vale (VALE3) are Highlighted
medium.summary: Empiricus Research highlighted the challenging domestic market environment, with Ibovespa falling from near 200,000 points in April to around 177,000 currently. The market now expects Selic to end 2026 at 13.25% according to the latest Focus report. The research house issued tactical adjustment alerts for its recommended stocks, particularly focusing on Petrobras and Vale for income generation strategies amid the deteriorating outlook.

medium.title: Raízen (RAIZ4), Petrobras (PETR4), Azul (AZUL3) and Other Highlights This Wednesday (27)
medium.summary: Raízen is advancing in negotiations with creditors over its R$ 65 billion debt, with a deadline of June 9 to present a recovery plan requiring 50%+1 creditor approval. The company may already have the necessary quorum from local creditors but still seeks bondholder support, who hold about 40% of the debt. Petrobras responded about interest in Refit's terrain, and Azul debuted on NYSE.
